correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, a positive support dominates exactly when it meets at least two parts or fills one whole part. This makes the one-guard transfer rule depend only on the number of supported parts, the total guard weight in each supported part and the number of zeros left there. The three support cases in RESULT.md follow directly. I independently compared the literal transfer rule to the theorem criterion on every ordered multipartite composition through order seven, totaling 164682 labelings, with zero mismatches; an independent polynomial reconstruction also matched every brute-force weight histogram through order six. The packaged verifier extends the finite stress test through order eight.
risks: Finite enumeration corroborates rather than proves the arbitrary-order theorem; the support argument is the proof.

value.rationale: A complete feasible-function classification strictly refines a known scalar domination number and yields every weight coefficient for a canonical graph family. The exact two-supported-part obstruction is structurally reusable, so this is more than a routine minimum computation.

final_claim: All weak Roman dominating functions of an arbitrary connected complete multipartite graph admit the stated support/partwise-weight classification, yielding the closed weak Roman weight enumerator in RESULT.md; the known minimum weak Roman number is only a corollary and is not the originality-bearing claim.
limitations: No repeated-attack, foolproof or total weak Roman variant.
